Is that fetched automatically like the `.debugsymbols` file? Is it an alternative to the debug symbols or a replacement?

We have this rename check for the `.debugsymbols` file to ensure renames work, not sure if that works out of the box with the `.pdb` file, I haven't built with msvc lately so can't test currently but can set up and test
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c12e51972a41665743be79c7d3e3fd5c871d97f3/platform/windows/crash_handler_windows_signal.cpp#L271-L273

Would this need a different check for that case?

> Is it an alternative to the debug symbols or a replacement?

It's an alternative; you can't have both `.debugsymbols` and `.pdb` for a single build.

Note that MSVC debug symbols are *always* separate as `.pdb`, while MinGW debug symbols can be embedded into the `.exe`.

> Would this need a different check for that case?

Yes, as this check is only intended to find separate MinGW debug symbols.

There is another issue we'll probably need to tackle with MSVC debug symbols: the executable finds the PDB location with a path defined in the `.exe`, which is written as absolute in Godot. This means that if you export the project to any location that isn't the same path as the location the project was built, the debug symbols won't be recognized automatically.

@bruvzg	Any ideas?
Then I think we can leave that as a follow-up including code to integrate that into the system (official builds are made with gcc so will only be relevant for custom builds with msvc)

Official templates are not using MSVC, so I think it's OK to skip it for now.

I think path can be set to relative using `/PDBALTPATH:`, but it still will need change when exporting.
See `WindowsUtils::copy_and_rename_pdb` which is doing the PDB renaming for GDExtension dlls, something similar probably can be done for the export.

So my main question is how we're going to distribute `.debugsymbols` files, as they're quite heavy.

We may want to distribute them as zip files and keep them as zip files in the templates folder, to minimize disk usage for the user, and unzip them at export time. If so, we'd need to add the unzipping logic here.

A quick test on 4.8-dev3:
```
-rwxr-xr-x. 1 akien akien 901M Aug 18 17:40 godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols
-rw-r--r--. 1 akien akien 320M Aug 18 19:14 godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols.zip
-rw-r--r--. 1 akien akien 311M Aug 18 19:15 godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols.7zip.zip
```

So ~300M instead of 900M when zipped with `zip` or `7z`.
That makes sense to separate out, but we'd need to support both and unsure how we'd handle that specifically

I'd say:
```
if not exists debug_symbols_path and exists debug_symbols_path + ".zip":
  extract zip to tmp folder
  debug_symbols_path = tmp folder/file

use debug_symbols_path
```

That's assuming `debug_symbols_path` can be either sourced from installed export templates or from a custom debug/release template. If it's only for installed export templates then we'd only need to support whichever format we ship them as.

Some more compression tests btw:
- `xz`, default settings:
```
-rw-r--r--. 1 akien akien 200M Aug 19 09:22 godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols.xz
```
- `zstd`:
```
$ zstd -3 godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols
godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols : 33.32%   (   901 MiB =>    300 MiB, godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols.zst)
$ zstd -10 godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols
godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols : 30.36%   (   901 MiB =>    273 MiB, godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols.zst)
$ zstd -19 godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols
godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols : 24.42%   (   901 MiB =>    220 MiB, godot.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.debugsymbols.zst)
```
(`3` is the default and very fast to compress, `19` is the max and pretty slow, but still acceptable for server side compression if decompression stays fast)

xz/lzma gives the best compression for Linux debug symbols it seems, but I don't think we support it in Godot. zstd with a high compression ratio (maybe 15 or so? would need to compare decompression speed) might be the best option.

It might be reasonable to provide debug symbols per-target as unlike export templates you're probably most likely going to only need one or a few targets in most cases, i.e. when testing locally, and if users are bundling the symbols with shipped debug versions (or even release versions) then it wouldn't be a major hurdle I'd say to download them separately, 18 gb for mostly platforms you don't need might be a hurdle otherwise (we can still provide one and have individual download support like we have for the templates though for integration with the download manager, though we'd still need to consider the feasibility and stability of uploading to the host, restart time, etc.)

From a user perspective we'd probably mostly care about the editor interface for downloads though so I think infrastructure is more critical there

Another alternative would be one pack for debug and one for release, as I'd say it's far more likely users are interested in the debug template symbols only

But that's largely a follow-up discussion

I'll look at implementing specifically zip and if we decide to add other compression support to improve ratio we can follow-up with that I'd say (as well as integrating template download support for the export template manager)
When I've implemented zip support I'll also test out integrating that into my own build workflow to verify with that format as well
